prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
[goal] A single-file Win95-style archery game in ./game/index.html: mouse aim, hold-to-draw power, poppable balloons, on-screen score, start and lose conditions.

[action] Wrote the whole game in one HTML file (canvas rendering, WebAudio synth SFX, no build step, no external assets), then opened it in the browser and played one shot to verify.

[result]
- File: game/index.html, self-contained.
- Verified live in the browser: start screen renders (title, START button, instructions); clicking START starts the game; HUD shows "SCORE 0 / 15" and "ARROWS LEFT 5"; balloons drift across the sky; holding the mouse draws the bow with a power bar and dotted trajectory preview; releasing fired an arrow that popped a balloon and the score went to "SCORE 1 / 15".
- Close the tab I opened (done, now on about:blank).

How it plays:
- Aim with the mouse; hold to draw (power builds 0→1), release to shoot. Arrow has gravity, so you lead moving targets.
- Win: pop 15 balloons. Lose: miss 5 arrows (arrow hits ground or leaves the screen).
- Feel/sound: draw creak, bow "thwip" + noise on release, per-balloon pitched pop with burst particles and "+1" floater, "MISS" floater, win arpeggio, lose descending tone. Retro Courier HUD, sky/hills/sun/clouds backdrop, stick archer with animated bow.

Assumptions I made (brief left these open):
- Win = 15 pops, lose = 5 misses (stated on the start screen).
- Balloons drift horizontally at varied speeds/heights; ~5 on screen at once.
- Single level, no timer; "lose" is purely miss-based.
- Audio via WebAudio (no files), so it works offline with only Google Fonts reachable.

Evidence it's right: I opened the file, clicked START, drew and released, and observed the score increment from 0 to 1 after a balloon pop — the full aim/draw/shoot/hit/score loop works. No build step; it runs from a plain file:// URL.

[next] None — first complete version delivered and verified; browser tab closed.
